feedback.problem: Consider a matrix equation $A\,x={B}^{-1}\,d,$ where $A$ and $B$ are $2\times 2$ non-singular matrices, while $x$ and $d$ are $2\times 1$ column vectors. Solve the equation for $x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $A$ is not singular, it must have an inverse ${A}^{-1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $A\,x={B}^{-1}\,d$ by ${A}^{-1},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A\,x & ={B}^{-1}\,d \\ {A}^{-1}A\,x & ={A}^{-1}{B}^{-1}\,d \\ {I}_{2}\,x & ={A}^{-1}{B}^{-1}\,d \\ x & ={A}^{-1}{B}^{-1}\,d.\end{aligned}
$$
